problems: The pink flower sits on the grass in storyboard frames 1-2. From frame 3 on it hangs in mid-air at head height beside the character, with no stem in the ground and nothing holding it. It floats there for the rest of the film (all three full-size frames).
A plain beige rectangular block sticks through the front of the character's body in every frame. It looks like a post clipping through the figure, not part of it.
The throw is barely there: an arm flicks in frames 3-4. The stone is at most a dark speck (frame 4, at-50), so nobody can see it leave the hand or fly.

The rings are hard, perfectly even white ovals with no splash and no disturbance in the water. In at-75 several stack closely, so they read as flat hoops lying on the sea rather than ripples. The caption's 'thin rings' fits, but they look pasted on.

The order of the rings does not show a stone hopping outward. The first ring appears at mid distance (frame 5) and the later ones near the horizon (frames 9-16). There is no first contact close to the shore, so the 'hopped' path cannot be followed.
The title says 'a take that misses', but nothing in the film shows what missed or reads as a failure. The film just ends with rings fading (frame 16).
posts.critique: Someone scrolling sees a figure from behind with a flower floating beside its head and a post stuck through its body, then white hoops appearing on the sea with no visible stone, splash or cause. The throw and the miss in the title never come across, and the floating flower and the clipping block are the first things a viewer notices.
